lead.label: 4j
lead.why: Abstract: 'Among the synthesized compounds, the most potent compound was compound 4j with eightfold higher inhibitory activity compared to acarbose.'

reactions.conditions: One-pot three-component reaction: aldehyde (1 mmol), aminopyrazole 2 (1 mmol), isocyanide (1.2 mmol), NH4Cl (20 mol%), toluene (10 mL), reflux 8 h; evaporate, recrystallise from n-hexane. Yield 81%. Atmospheric oxidation implied (mechanism: 'under further oxidation').
reactions.source: Main text, Chemistry section, Scheme 1, Experimental 'Procedure for the synthesis of imidazo[1,2-b]pyrazoles 4a-o' and compound 4j entry; no SI used

notes: The aldehyde and isocyanide for 4j are not named in the text; they were derived from the product name (4-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl at C2 and cyclohexylimino at C3), and the Table 1 drawing was not visible in the text layer. The paper states only generally that reagents were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich and Merck; aminopyrazole 2 has no preparation in the paper. Atom balance: C27H28N4O4 = aldehyde C8H8O3 + aminopyrazole C12H13N3O2 + isocyanide C7H11N - H2O - 2H (oxidation).
